_: V90Phase4Demodulator::reset, against t_v90p4ddec's run_p4d_reset.
Eleven stores, seven calls, two diagnostics and a loop.  The claims worth
attacking are WHICH field each store reaches and WHICH of the four
arguments it takes; WHICH record the session flag resets and the ONE
asymmetry between those two arms; WHICH block the demapper and the
converter are given; WHICH parameter `quickConnect` selects; and WHICH
decision member the loop runs.
ANCHORS ARE EXTENDED BACKWARDS UNTIL THEY MATCH ONCE (findings 7432 and
7459).  Six of the eleven stores are spelled identically in
`resetBeforRRN`, `detectRRN`, `detectFPE` and the three `enterWaitFor*`,
and both `state = ...; countInState = 0;` pairs appear a dozen times in
the two decision members.  The lines unique to `reset` are `ucode =
code;`, `int_3510 = 0;`, the two `rDetector*.reset(` calls,
`quickConnect = quickConnectArg;`, the `groupSize` triple, the
`phase4Modulator.` pair and the loop.
TWO CLAIMS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ATTACKED HERE, and the reason is that no
input can present them.  The demapper's reset is guarded on
`mappingParams1` and on `autoDigitalImpDetector`, and BOTH pointers are
dereferenced unconditionally elsewhere in the same function -- the first
at `mappingParams1->word_0` before the guard, the second at
`autoDigitalImpDetector->pcmType` after it -- so a null value for either
is a segfault and not a trial.  A mutation dropping either test is
EQUIVALENT over every object this class can be given, and one is not
written rather than written and excused.
